[frame] function TextTransparencyFade(element, totalframes, fadein)
[frame] 		local transincrement = (1 - element.TextTransparency) / totalframes
[frame] 		local strokeincrement = (1 - element.TextStrokeTransparency) / totalframes
[frame] 			if i < totalframes then

[frame] 			element.TextStrokeTransparency = 1 - (strokeincrement * totalframes)
[frame] 	end),element, totalframes, fadein)

[frame] local function cframe(obj)
[frame]         return obj and (obj:IsA("BasePart") and obj.CFrame or obj:IsA("Model") and obj:GetModelCFrame())
[frame]                 local edgeCFrame = cframe(object) * CFrame.new((size(object) / 2) * combined)
[frame]                 edges[index] = {edgeCFrame, edgeSize}
[frame]                         local vertexCFrame = v.CFrame:toWorldSpace(CFrame.new(vertexOffset));
[frame]                         maxX = math.max(maxX, vertexCFrame.X)
[frame]                         minX = math.min(minX, vertexCFrame.X)
[frame]                         maxY = math.max(maxY, vertexCFrame.Y)
[frame]                         minY = math.min(minY, vertexCFrame.Y)
[frame]                         maxZ = math.max(maxZ, vertexCFrame.Z)
[frame]                         minZ = math.min(minZ, vertexCFrame.Z)
[frame]         local cframe = CFrame.new(Vector3.new(maxX+minX, maxY+minY, maxZ+minZ)/2)
[frame]         return size,cframe

[frame] function GetCFrame(object)--we'll get a CFrame value out of a CFrameValue or a StringValue formatted like a CFrame
[frame] 	if object:IsA("CFrameValue") then--if someone is using a CFrame value then we'll just pull the value directly
[frame] 	elseif object:IsA("StringValue") then--added functionality for this because I dislike interfacing with CFrame values
[frame] 		local cframe = nil
[frame] 			cframe = CFrame.new(object.Value:match("(.+),(.+),(.+),(.+),(.+),(.+),(.+),(.+),(.+),(.+),(.+),(.+)"))
[frame] 			--if you print your CFrame and paste it into the string value, this will find that out and use it properly
[frame] 		return cframe
[frame] 			local DoorCFrameValue = MatchingDoor:FindFirstChild("DoorCFrame")
[frame] 			local HingeCFrameValue = MatchingDoor:FindFirstChild("HingeCFrame")
[frame] 			if DoorCFrameValue and HingeCFrameValue then
[frame] 				local doorCFrame = GetCFrame(DoorCFrameValue)
[frame] 				local hingeCFrame = GetCFrame(HingeCFrameValue)
[frame] 				if doorCFrame and hingeCFrame then
[frame] 					MakeDoor(i,MatchingDoor,hingeCFrame,doorCFrame)
[frame] 		leftMotor.C0 = CFrame.new(-WheelSize/2-Left.Size.x/2,0,0)*CFrame.Angles(math.pi/2,0,-math.pi/2)
[frame] 		leftMotor.C1 = CFrame.new(Base.Size.x/2+Left.Size.x+WheelSize/2,0,0)*CFrame.Angles(math.pi/2,0,math.pi/2)
[frame] 		rightMotor.C0 = CFrame.new(-WheelSize/2-Right.Size.x/2,0,0)*CFrame.Angles(math.pi/2,0,math.pi/2)
[frame] 		rightMotor.C1 = CFrame.new(-Base.Size.x/2-Right.Size.x-WheelSize/2,0,0)*CFrame.Angles(math.pi/2,0,math.pi/2)

[frame] function GetCFrame(object)--we'll get a CFrame value out of a CFrameValue or a StringValue formatted like a CFrame
[frame] 	if object:IsA("CFrameValue") then--if someone is using a CFrame value then we'll just pull the value directly
[frame] 	elseif object:IsA("StringValue") then--added functionality for this because I dislike interfacing with CFrame values

[frame] 			--if you print your CFrame and paste it into the string value, this will find that out and use it properly
[frame] 		return cframe
